title: Southern elephant seal resighting histories, Macquarie Island, 1950s study (cohorts 1951-1965): seal years 1951-1985, breeding season and rest-of-year occasions
creator: Volzke, Sophia (University of Tasmania); McMahon, Clive R.; Hindell, Mark A.; Burton, Harry R.; Wotherspoon, Simon J.
citation: Volzke, S. (2023). Macquarie Island southern elephant seal capture-mark-recapture data [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.zpc866t7f
abstract: Resighting histories of 7531 southern elephant seals marked as weaned pups on the Macquarie Island isthmus (cohorts 1951-1965) and resighted by organised island searches (1952, 1959) and opportunistic sightings to 1979, with a handful of sightings to 1986. Built from the deposited sighting records: one row per seal x seal year (September to August) x occasion (1 = breeding season, September-October; 2 = the rest of the seal year), y = 1 if the seal was recorded in that window, y_raw = number of distinct sighting days. The survey set is inferred from the sightings themselves (a window is surveyed if any marked seal of this study was sighted in it); per-window sighting counts are in __periods so sparse windows can be dropped. Each seal's rows begin in its cohort (marking) year.
samplingProtocol: Permanent marking of weaned pups (hot-iron branding, 1951-1965) and resighting of marked seals ashore: by organised island searches (1952, 1959) and opportunistic sightings to 1979, with a handful of sightings to 1986. Sightings record date, sex, age class, breeding status and moult stage.
surveyEvidenceNote: No effort table is deposited and the papers do not list which seasons were searched. A period x occasion window is in the survey set iff at least one marked seal of this study has a sighting record in it; every unit then carries a row for that window. Windows with very few sightings (see __periods n_sightings_*) reflect ad hoc effort and may be dropped before fitting; the 2021 paper's analysis windows were 1957-1979 and 1993-2003.
closureNote: occasion within period (two resight windows per seal year; the papers treat a breeding-season sighting as a breeding event and a rest-of-year sighting as alive, nonbreeding or unknown); open between seal years (CJS / multi-state)

occasionCodes.1: breeding season, September-October of `year` (the papers' 'seen breeding' emission)
occasionCodes.2: rest of the seal year, November of `year` to August of `year`+1 (the papers' 'seen other' emission; moult, mid-year haul-out)

geographicCoverage: Macquarie Island, Southern Ocean (54.5 S, 158.9 E); all seals marked on the isthmus; no coordinates deposited
notes: Units are seals whose first record is a pup age class (01-05); their first record's seal year is unit_cohort_year, and as seals marked at birth (E4.4) they have no rows before it. unit_tag_type is NA where the deposit has #N/A (every 1950s seal, although the README says they were branded). unit_sex U = never sexed. y_raw counts distinct sighting days (163 same-day duplicate records in the deposit collapsed). Per-sighting breeding status, age class, moult and weight are not shipped; a multi-state breeding history can be rebuilt from the deposit's SEAL_STATUS_ID.

notShipped.seals first recorded past the pup stage: 7 seals (both studies: 2,282) with no known cohort; the 2021 paper also excludes seals first tagged as adults
notShipped.other study: the other mark-recapture study in the same file is the sibling table
notShipped.per-sighting attributes: SEAL_STATUS_ID, AGE_CLASS_ID, MOULT_ID, WEIGHT, SEX_ON_SIGHTING, SEAL_TAGS_ON_ANIMAL, COMMENTS and data-entry columns
notShipped.sightings outside the study's seal years: none: the 1950s cohorts' last sighting is in seal year 1985 and the 1990s cohorts' first is 1984
